question.problem:
John is selling juice at a market stall. The table below gives the rate $r(t)$ of juice sold over a period of $6$ hours, from $1\,\text{p.m.}$ to $7\,\text{p.m.}$

| $t\,(\text{hours})$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $r(t)\,(\text{liters/hour})$ | $k$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |

If the left Riemann sum approximation of the total number of liters John sold during the given period has a value of $16$ liters, what is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the curve $y=r(t)$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{r({t}_{0})+r({t}_{1})+…+r({t}_{n-1})}})\cdot \,\,{{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{ }\text{width}} \\  & =(r(1)+r(3)+r(5))\cdot Δt.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $r(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $r(t)$ | $k$ | $2$ | $3$ |

So, we obtain the following approximation to the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(k+2+3)\cdot 2 \\  & =2(k+5) \\  & =2k+10\end{aligned}
$$

In the given context, the area under the curve represents the total number of liters sold by John. Since we are given that the left Riemann sum approximation of the total number of liters sold is $16,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2k+10 & =16 \\ 2k & =6 \\ k & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
